n: Alma’s preaching bears fruit: many believe, begin to repent, and start searching the scriptures for themselves.
But most want to kill Alma and Amulek — angry at Alma’s plain words to Zeezrom and accusing Amulek of lying and insulting their law, lawyers, and judges.
Stung by plain testimony against their wickedness, they plot to kill the missionaries secretly.
Instead they tie them with strong cords and take them before the chief judge of the land.
Witnesses accuse them — twisting their words about God and Christ, just as Zeezrom had done earlier.
Zeezrom is shocked at how his own lies have blinded the people. Torn by guilt, he feels encircled by the pains of hell.

f.g: Torn and tormented, like ground broken by a harrow.

n: Zeezrom publicly confesses his guilt and declares Alma and Amulek innocent. The crowd accuses him of being possessed, spits on him, and drives him and the other believers out, throwing stones after them.

f.w: I am guilty, and these men are spotless before God

n: In one of scripture’s darkest scenes, they burn the believers’ wives and children — and burn the scriptures as well.

f.g: An attempt to destroy both the believers and the word of God they followed.

n: Alma and Amulek are forced to watch the martyrdom.

f.g: Martyr comes from the Greek word for “witness.”

n: Amulek, anguished, urges Alma to use God’s power to save them from the flames.

f.w: How can we witness this awful scene
f.g: An honest cry many people echo when the innocent suffer.

n: Alma says the Spirit restrains him. The Lord is receiving the victims into glory, and allows the evil so his coming judgments will be just; innocent blood will witness against the murderers.

f.w: the Lord receiveth them up unto himself, in glory

n: Amulek fears they too might be burned.

f.w: perhaps they will burn us also
f.g: An understandable fear for a new missionary.

n: Alma submits to God’s will, yet feels assured their work isn’t finished, so they will not be burned.

f.w: Be it according to the will of the Lord

f.g: Compare Joseph Smith’s similar confidence that he would be preserved until his work was done.

n: After the burning, the chief judge slaps them and taunts them: will you still preach about a lake of fire and brimstone?

f.w: smote them with his hand upon their cheeks

n: He mocks that neither they nor God saved the believers, strikes them again, and demands an answer.
Mormon notes this judge followed the order of Nehor — the same priestcraft that had killed Gideon.

f.w: the order and faith of Nehor

n: Alma and Amulek say nothing. The judge strikes them again and sends them to prison.
After three days, lawyers, judges, priests, and teachers of Nehor’s order come to question them, but they stay silent.
The judge threatens them with burning and commands them to speak; they still say nothing.

f.w: I have power to deliver you up

n: Day after day the mockers return, slapping them and taunting: if you have such power, why not free yourselves?

f.w: why do ye not deliver yourselves

n: They gnash their teeth, spit on them, and mock their message: “How shall we look when we are damned?”
For many days they are mocked, starved, denied water, stripped naked, and kept bound.

f.g: Their suffering parallels that of Christ and his apostles.

n: On the twelfth day of the tenth month of the tenth year, the chief judge and many teachers and lawyers come to the prison.

f.w: the twelfth day, in the tenth month
f.g: Mormon preserves an exact date for this pivotal event.

n: The judge strikes them and dares them: if you have God’s power, free yourselves, and then we’ll believe God will destroy us.

f.g: A demand for a sign — which they will receive, at great cost.

n: One by one, each strikes them with the same taunt. When the last finishes, God’s power comes upon Alma and Amulek, and they stand.

f.w: the power of God was upon Alma and Amulek

n: Alma cries out: how long, O Lord? Give us strength according to our faith in Christ. They snap their cords, and their tormentors begin to flee.

f.w: according to our faith which is in Christ

n: Terrified, the people fall before reaching the door. The earth shakes, the prison walls split and fall, killing the chief judge, lawyers, priests, and teachers who had abused them.

f.w: the walls of the prison were rent in twain

n: Alma and Amulek walk out unharmed, freed by the power God gave them through faith in Christ. Everyone else inside is killed.
Crowds rush toward the noise, see the two men walking out of the fallen prison, and flee like a goat with her young fleeing two lions.

f.w: as a goat fleeth with her young from two lions
f.g: A vivid image of terror before overwhelming power.
